subject: Renewal + Capacity Scale: proposal for expanding Reserved pool to 32 GPUs
messages:
From: Elena Rivas <elena@novusai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 09:17 PST
Subject: Renewal planning: wanting to double Dedicated capacity at renewal

Hi Sergio,

Hope you’re well — our current Dedicated pool (16 GPUs) is in its final quarter and we’re kicking off renewal planning. After load testing on the new retrieval pipeline we estimate a sustained need that looks like a sprint to 32 GPUs by Q1 next year.

Primary asks from our side:
- Pricing for a 32 GPU reserved pool for 12 and 24 month terms (per-GPU hourly reserved rate and any blended ramp options)
- Any throughput guarantees you can commit to (p95 token latency targets we can rely on)
- Options for staged migration (we’d like a 30–60 day ramp window with mixed routing)

Can you send a short proposal and available SLO/credit language so our procurement team can budget and start escalation? We’d like to finalize commercial terms by end of month.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rivas
Head of Platform — NovusAI
elena@novusai.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena@novusai.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 10:03 PST
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: wanting to double Dedicated capacity at renewal

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks. We can absolutely support a staged upgrade to 32 GPUs and have a proposal draft for procurement. High level we can offer:

- 12-month term: commit to 32 GPUs with a staged 60-day ramp; per-GPU reserved rate: $8.25/hr after ramp (detailed below).
- 24-month term: lower per-GPU reserved rate $7.50/hr after ramp; additional 5% volume discount if billed annually in advance.
- Ramp/blend: first 30 days blended rate of $9.10/hr for newly-activated GPUs, second 30 days step-down to $8.25 (12mo) or $7.50 (24mo).
- Throughput SLO: p95 generation latency under 200ms for 2k context on the high-priority pool; SLO credits apply if we miss target.
- Operational: canary routing, KV-cache pre-warm, and optional cold-start burst lanes during ramp windows.

I’m copying Stephanie (pricing) and Dev (Dedicated ops) — we’ll circulate a formal PDF and the rate sheet later today. Would you be available for a 30-min alignment call tomorrow to walk procurement through the SLO language?

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 11:08 PST
Subject: RE: internal calc for NovusAI uplift pricing

Sergio / Stephanie — quick internal note before we send the external PDF. I ran the utilization model with the 32-GPU commit and two ramp profiles: 60-day staged vs immediate activation. Key numbers:

- 12mo commit (60d ramp): projected effective blended per-GPU/hr = $8.62 over first 90 days then $8.25 steady state.
- 24mo commit (60d ramp): projected blended = $7.95 over first 90 days then $7.50 steady state; cash-pay upfront reduces effective to ~$7.12.
- We can guarantee throughput SLO for the reserved pool given the pre-warm and KV-cache policy; if SLO is missed more than twice in a rolling month, we should offer service credit equal to 5% of monthly reserved spend per breach (capped at 25%).

I’ve attached the rate sheet and a suggested SOW language. Also note: adding 16 GPUs to an existing pool requires a short maintenance window for sharding (we recommend a 2-hour low-traffic window).

—Dev

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena@novusai.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21 08:44 PST
Subject: Proposal: Reserved Pool uplift to 32 GPUs (NovusAI) — terms and SLOs (v3)

Elena — attaching the formal proposal (NovusAI_renewal_proposal_v3.pdf) and the rate sheet. Key commercial terms summarized here:

SUMMARY
- Requested change: increase Dedicated reserved pool from 16 -> 32 GPUs.
- Recommended term options: 12 months or 24 months.

PRICING (per-GPU reserved hour)
- 12-month term: $8.25/hr (post-ramp); 60-day ramp with blended start: first 30 days new GPUs at $9.10/hr, next 30 days step-down to $8.25/hr.
- 24-month term: $7.50/hr (post-ramp); same ramp; 5% discount available for annual prepayment.

SLO / SERVICE CREDITS
- SLO: p95 generation latency < 200ms for 2k tokens on the priority routing.
- Credits: 5% of monthly reserved spend per qualifying SLO breach, up to 25% cap; two breaches allowed in a rolling month before crediting triggers.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
- Staged migration: we’ll route 25% traffic to the new capacity week 1, 50% week 2, 75% week 3, 100% week 5.
- Pre-warm window and KV-cache seeding included. One maintenance sharding window (2 hours) required for the final add.

NEXT STEPS
1) Procurement: confirm term (12 vs 24 mo) and whether you want annual prepayment.
2) We’ll issue an amendment + SOW; I’ll route a DocuSign link for signature once you confirm.
3) Coordinate migration weekend window (we suggest weekend of Dec 18) — ops will share availability.

We’re flexible on a limited amount of concession if needed to close: e.g., a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs. Full details in the attached.

Regards,
Sergio

Attachments: NovusAI_renewal_proposal_v3.pdf; NovusAI_RateCard_v2.xlsx; SOW_NovusAI_renewal.docx

From: Elena Rivas <elena@novusai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>
Date: 2026-11-23 14:12 PST
Subject: Re: Proposal: Reserved Pool uplift to 32 GPUs (NovusAI) — terms and SLOs (v3)

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the clear summary and attachments. Procurement reviewed and has two asks:

1) Can you reduce the blended ramp rate for the first 30 days? They’re pushing back on the $9.10/hr line item. A blended cap of $8.50/hr for the first 30 days would make the internal budget comfortable.
2) SLO credits: procurement wants the credit to apply after a single qualifying breach (not two), and a higher cap (up to 40% monthly reserved spend) for the first 3 months while we stabilize.

If you can accept a modest concession on 1) and adjust credit terms on 2) for an initial stabilization period, we can sign and target an activation window in mid-December.

Would you be able to share a revised redline by tomorrow?

—Elena

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena@novusai.com>
Cc: NovusAI Procurement <procurement@novusai.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25 15:04 PST
Subject: Re: Proposal: Reserved Pool uplift to 32 GPUs (NovusAI) — terms and SLOs (v3)

Elena — thanks for the quick review. We’re willing to make the following limited, time-bound concessions to accelerate signing: 

- Ramp first 30 days blended cap reduced to $8.50/hr (from $9.10). Effective post-ramp rates remain $8.25 (12mo) / $7.50 (24mo).
- SLO credits: for months 1–3 we’ll trigger credits after a single qualifying breach; credit = 7% of monthly reserved spend per breach, capped at 40% for that stabilization window. From month 4 onward, revert to standard terms (5% per breach, capped at 25%, and two-breach grace period).
- One-time onboarding credit: $12,000 applied on first invoice if signed by Nov 30.

If that sounds acceptable I’ll prepare an amendment and route a DocuSign for signatures (link included: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc-req-2026nv). Ops (Dev & Lauren) will follow up on the migration weekend schedule and exact sharding window.

Appreciate the partnership — happy to jump on a 15-min call to close this out.

Best,
Sergio
